attemptUniqueness.ownerAuthority: the `attempts` table declares PRIMARY KEY (project_id, attempt_id)
attemptUniqueness.projectorBehavior: the ATTEMPT_CREATED projector INSERT is wrapped so a duplicate raises ProjectionError('attempt already exists')
attemptUniqueness.conclusion: the canonical owner already enforces Attempt uniqueness; the consumer's `.find()` is NOT a second authority
attemptUniqueness.consumerCheckAdded: a DEFENSIVE duplicate-count check in admitAttempt raises ATTEMPT_SOURCE_CONFLICT if more than one canonical ATTEMPT_CREATED names the same attempt in one project — a cheap integrity assertion, not a new authority

readIntegrityLayers.rowToEvent: validates and parses each stored row
readIntegrityLayers.verifyFull: the owner's full event-chain validation (per-project sequence, previous-digest linkage, causation-earlier)
readIntegrityLayers.consumerAdmission: reads the project-scoped event list and requires exactly one matching ATTEMPT_CREATED
readIntegrityLayers.buildProjectTrajectory: re-parses each Work event and recomputes both digests

failedProjectionHandling.before: every T0 projection failure collapsed into one 'could not be built' caveat, so a corrupted canonical Work source was indistinguishable from an uncomposed optional owner
failedProjectionHandling.after: a TrajectoryRefusal (T0's own Work-history validation refusal) is reported as a CANONICAL WORK SOURCE integrity failure; any other failure is reported as an optional cross-owner plane that could not be projected
failedProjectionHandling.canonicalFactsUnaffected: the canonical Work facts come from the owner's own read, so they are not lost when the projection fails; the PROJECT CONTEXT is what degrades, and it now says why
